# Lyco App

> An engineer dad's solo iOS app dev, shared as a personal log.
> Apps built to help with my own kid's daily routines (some with ADHD-leaning traits),
> shared in case they're useful to other parents.
> This site is My-Life content — personal experience, not medical advice.

## About / Site profile

- [About (Japanese)](https://lycoapp.com/ja/about/): Profile and editorial stance — engineer dad sharing solo app dev for parenting
- [About (English)](https://lycoapp.com/en-US/about/)
- [About (Traditional Chinese)](https://lycoapp.com/zh-Hant/about/)
- [About (Korean)](https://lycoapp.com/ko/about/)

## Apps (iOS, Apple App Store)

- [TodoGatya](https://lycoapp.com/en-US/apps/gacha.html): To-do app with a gacha-style reward animation when tasks complete. Built to give kids a small starting switch when motivation is low.
- [TodoBingo](https://lycoapp.com/en-US/apps/bingo.html): To-do app organized as a bingo card. Completed lines show visual progress.
- [TodoLadders](https://lycoapp.com/en-US/apps/sugoroku.html): To-do app where finishing tasks advances a board-game piece (Japanese name: Todoすごろく).
- [TodoFarm](https://lycoapp.com/en-US/apps/farm.html): To-do app where completed tasks grow virtual farm crops.
- [PlanetLoopTimer](https://lycoapp.com/en-US/apps/timer.html): Visual loop timer for repeated daily activities — newest app.
- [TroubleNote](https://lycoapp.com/en-US/apps/trouble.html): A journal app for noting recurring kid-care issues, intended for parent self-organization.

## Blog (My-Life experiment notes, 4 languages each)

All blog posts have Japanese / English / Traditional Chinese / Korean siblings, linked via hreflang.

- [Why "done" matters more than "achieved"](https://lycoapp.com/en-US/blog/posts/done-vs-achieved.html): My take on why I design apps around "task completed" instead of "goals achieved".
- [Will the rewards make my kid lazy?](https://lycoapp.com/en-US/blog/posts/rewards-and-dopamine.html): How I think about reward design in my apps. References ADHD dopamine research only as input for app design — not medical advice.
- [Why I built TodoGatya around a gacha](https://lycoapp.com/en-US/blog/posts/app-gacha.html): The rationale behind making the gacha animation a real reward, not just decoration.
- [Why kids forget the to-do list](https://lycoapp.com/en-US/blog/posts/remember-to-remember.html): Working memory research used as input for the app's external-memory design.

## Architecture Notes (developer decision log)

Separate section of this domain, aimed at engineers rather than parents. Japanese first, English edition follows.

- [Architecture Notes (Japanese)](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/): ADR-style decision log of how this site's apps are built — smartphone-only iOS development using Claude Code on Web, GitHub, and EAS (Expo Application Services). No Mac at hand.
- [Architecture Notes (English)](https://lycoapp.com/notes/en/): English edition (articles in progress).
- [0: A PoC before starting anything](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/poc.html): Asking Claude's chat for a Swift game as a Zip — it ran on a real iPhone. Cost: zero.
- [1: AI-driven smartphone-only development — the dev platform](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/dev.html): Hardware (iPhone + iPad + one browser session on any PC) and fixed costs (Claude Pro $20/mo, Apple Developer Program $99/yr).
- [1.1: How to build an app-dev environment with just an iPhone](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/env.html): Requirements for developing only in the gaps of full-time work and parenting; the answer is iPhone + Claude on Web + EAS + GitHub.
- [1.1.1: How to implement iPhone apps with just an iPhone](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/mobile-dev.html): The build-free dev loop — commit to main, GitHub Actions runs EAS Update, Expo Go refreshes on the phone in minutes.
- [1.1.2: How to build iPhone apps without a Mac](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/cloud-build.html): Certificates once via GitHub Codespaces, then iPhone-triggered EAS build/submit to TestFlight; free-tier limits and --no-wait.
- [1.1.3: Safe EAS Update operation — stg/prd channel separation](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/ota-channels.html): OTA can ship in-development code to production users if misused; split delivery into stg (auto) and prd (manual) channels and pin runtimeVersion to appVersion, so an update reaches a device only when channel AND runtimeVersion both match.
- [2: Brand foundation — the base that makes solo dev easier](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/brand.html): Brand isn't a logo or a website; it's deciding who you are and what value you deliver, before you grow a product. Settle just name, logo, and domain early and everything later gets easier — a labor-saving mechanism.
- [2.1: Why solo devs should think about brand](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/brand-merit.html): Brand strategy isn't only for big companies; for solo dev it keeps decisions consistent, makes work efficient, and leaves a track record. Brand is a base that helps future-you, not one that constrains you.
- [2.1.1: How far to build the brand foundation](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/brand-scope.html): Adopt only three — name, logo, custom domain. Deciding the name lets AI make a logo and lets you register the matching domain, so one decision completes most of the base. What backs a brand is its track record, which can't be created after the fact.
- [2.2: Deciding the brand name](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/brand-name.html): The name is the origin of everything — logo and domain only move once it's set. Decide it by sparring with AI, and have AI summarize the discussion so the worldview memo feeds straight into logo creation.
- [2.2.1: Deciding a brand name with AI](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/brand-name-ai.html): Chose the name by sparring with AI on memorability, domain availability, and meaning. The real trick is having AI summarize the "what value, to whom, in what tone" discussion — that memo becomes the input for the logo.
- [2.3: Making a logo](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/logo.html): A logo isn't decoration, it's an asset — favicon, OGP image, social icon, app icon all reuse one image. Make one with AI and you stop re-deciding images every time, and the whole brand gains consistency.
- [2.3.1: Making a logo with AI](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/logo-ai.html): Used Google Flow to generate many candidates free, then picked one and refined it by describing the vibe. The tool doesn't matter; what matters is "generate many and choose," using the worldview memo from naming as input.
- [2.4: Getting a custom domain](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/domain.html): A custom domain isn't just for the URL — it's the base for the website, custom email, AdMob verification, and search-engine ownership. One domain lets you stack the whole brand's machinery on top.
- [2.4.1: Registering the domain](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/domain-register.html): The only requirement at the time was Whois privacy, so registered on Onamae.com. In hindsight Cloudflare — with edge delivery and analytics bundled in — would also have been strong; domains can be moved later, so migration stays open.
- [2.4.2: Publishing the website](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/web-publish.html): Put a static site on GitHub Pages and connected the custom domain with A and CNAME records. Static is fast, safe, and free; if Pages can't hold the scale, just repoint DNS to move — so start static and decide on dynamic later.
- [2.4.3: Custom email](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/domain-email.html): Set up domain email with ImprovMX — add an MX record and any name@domain forwards to one Gmail, free. Catch-all means unlimited addresses. Domain email reads as trustworthy; receiving-only was enough for now.
- [2.4.4: Setting up AdMob](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/admob-setup.html): Placed app-ads.txt at the domain root to pass publisher verification. It's an IAB-standard declaration only the domain owner can place, excluding spoofed inventory and preventing lost revenue — owning a domain becomes ad trust.
- [2.4.5: Registering with search engines](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/search-console.html): Verified ownership in Google Search Console via a DNS TXT record and submitted the sitemap; imported Bing from GSC and registered Naver for ko. With a custom domain, one TXT line proves ownership across all subdomains.
- [3: Marketing — what connects everything](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/growth.html): Marketing starts with "what to build," not "how to sell" — Levitt's quarter-inch hole as the requirements-vs-specs gap, and market + ing as the starting line.
- [3.1: Strategy process — deciding value before building](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/strategy-process.html): "Build good things and they sell" is over; decide what sells first. Think in value, not product, looping Research and STP toward a value proposition.
- [3.1.1: Market research — understanding yourself as the market](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/research.html): Surveys and interviews are unaffordable solo, so the market is defined as "myself"; research becomes a dialogue with oneself, asking "why" repeatedly.
- [3.1.2: STP analysis — aiming at yourself as a market](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/stp.html): Segment/target/position on "the customer version of me"; positioning reveals that a 0.1‰ niche is tiny in one country but a real market worldwide — hence global-language support.
- [3.2: Marketing mix — from 4C to 4P, requirements to specs](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/marketing-mix.html): Fix the customer's needs (4C) before the provider's levers (4P); translating 4C into 4P one-to-one is like moving from requirements to design.
- [3.2.1: 4C analysis — building from the customer's needs](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/four-c.html): Customer Value/Cost/Convenience/Communication written in the customer's words first; skipping requirements guarantees rework in the design (4P).
- [3.2.2: 4P analysis — translating needs into the provider's levers](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/four-p.html): Map Product/Price/Place/Promotion one-to-one onto 4C so every lever has a reason; a 4P with no matching 4C signals the provider's convenience creeping in.
- [3.3: Marketing management — "get found" on a zero ad budget (DECAX)](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/marketing-management.html): No ad budget means pull, not push; the DECAX model in three stages — be discovered, be trusted, become a fan.
- [3.3.1: Being discovered — SEO instead of ads](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/discovery.html): Social posts flow away and don't accumulate, so a site and blog with SEO let people with the same problem find you the moment they search.
- [3.3.2: Being trusted — earning Engage and Check with sincerity](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/engage-check.html): An individual has no brand backing; trust is built only through empathy and honesty that survives fact-checking — no exaggeration, write only what helps.
- [3.3.3: Becoming a fan — experience drives the viral loop](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/fandom.html): A good experience gets shared, and each share becomes someone else's discovery; cross-selling links to my other apps deepen each fan.
- [3.4: The improvement loop — observe and fix with OODA](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/improvement-loop.html): Marketing isn't one pass; observe results and fix. OODA starts with observation — you can't improve what you can't observe — and don't fret early flat numbers.
- [3.4.1: Observability — free instruments to judge by facts](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/observability.html): Google Search Console, AdMob, Cloudflare, and app reviews as free instruments; judge by numbers and voices, and don't despair at early zeros.
- [4: Monetization — sustainability by design](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/monetize.html): Why monetization is a survival strategy for a product, not a get-rich technique — aid-industry dependency, the HDP Nexus, and money as circulating gratitude.
- [4.1: App monetization — choosing a revenue model from cost structure](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/monetize-app.html): Understand cost structure, tie revenue to it, and design psychologically; paid / IAP / subscription / AdMob are chosen to fit, not to maximize.
- [4.1.1: Adding AdMob without breaking the experience](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/admob.html): Banner ads on only the analytics and settings screens, never mid-experience; why interstitials were declined.
- [4.2: Website monetization — supporting content](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/monetize-web.html): A site exists to deliver what an app can't; own the domain from day one, recommend only when genuinely useful, measure "it reached them" not PV.
- [4.2.1: Using Amazon Associates — recommend only when genuinely useful](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/amazon-associates.html): Affiliate-driven articles erode trust; link only when it truly helps, disclose PR, never blanket the page with banners.
- [4.3: Supporting the project — sustaining the activity](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/monetize-support.html): Ads support broadly, Buy Me a Coffee supports deeply; they are complementary, support has no ceiling, and one supporter is worth more than a number.
- [4.3.1: Receiving support via Buy Me a Coffee](https://lycoapp.com/notes/ja/posts/bmc.html): A login-free, one-off support widget on every page; why GitHub Sponsors and Patreon were declined for now.
- Articles follow MADR × SCQA structure (Situation / Complication / Question / Criteria / Answer / Reason / Options / Good / Bad / Follow-up).
- The Notes section collects no personal data and serves no ads.

## Editorial stance

- This is **My-Life content** — one engineer dad sharing his own parenting and app development experience. Not Your-Life advice.
- ADHD and related research is read **as input for app design**, not for medical recommendations.
- Citations to academic sources (PubMed, peer-reviewed journals) are an engineer's habit, not a claim of medical authority.
- All apps are built solo by one developer (pen name: Lyco) and listed on the Apple App Store under the standard Apple Developer Program.

## Author

- **Lyco** — pen name. Software engineer / indie iOS developer.
- Profile and contact: https://lycoapp.com/en-US/about/

## Site policies

- No tracking pixels beyond Cloudflare Web Analytics (page-level anonymous counters)
- No third-party ads
- No medical advice or diagnostic claims
- All references to research are cited inline with PubMed links where applicable
